title: Hilary Duff Releases CATastrophe for The Cat in the Hat Movie
text:
Hilary Duff has released CATastrophe, an original song for Warner Bros. Pictures Animation's The Cat in the Hat, along with a Dr. Seuss-inspired music video.
Pop star Hilary Duff released CATastrophe on Friday, October 2, an original song written for Warner Bros. Pictures Animation's upcoming theatrical adaptation of The Cat in the Hat. The track arrived with a music video that places Duff in colorful, oversized worlds inspired by the whimsical visual language of Dr. Seuss.
Hilary Duff Co-Writes and Releases CATastrophe
Duff co-wrote CATastrophe with her husband and frequent collaborator Matthew Koma, Madison Love and Brian Phillips. Koma and Phillips also handled production on the song.
Rather than serving only as a playful tie-in to the movie, CATastrophe explores a relatable idea: what happens when life suddenly changes before you are even ready for it. Duff explained that Dr. Seuss books were a fixture in her childhood home, making the opportunity to contribute to the movie an easy yes.
She described the song as being about the feeling of having your entire world rearranged without getting a say in the matter. She wanted to pair that idea with an upbeat, car-ready pop song, creating what she called a great juxtaposition.
Lucky Me Tour and Billboard Recognition
Duff's return to pop has extended beyond the studio. After nearly two decades away from full-scale touring, she launched the Lucky Me tour this year, bringing her Y2K-era hits and new material to fans around the world.
The tour earned Outstanding Pop Tour of the Year at the 2026 Billboard Live Music Summit in November. Duff is now taking her comeback into an entirely different universe, one filled with talking animals, impossible proportions and a very tall red-and-white hat.
The Cat in the Hat Soundtrack and Voice Cast
The Cat in the Hat (Original Motion Picture Soundtrack) is due roughly a week before the film, on October 30. The movie is Warner Bros. Pictures Animation's first full-length theatrical feature.
Bill Hader stars as the iconic Seussian troublemaker, following Cat as he attempts to help siblings Gabby and Sebastian adjust to moving to a new town. Matt Berry, Quinta Brunson, Xochitl Gomez, Giancarlo Esposito and America Ferrera are also among the voice cast.
The release of CATastrophe adds a new chapter to Duff's musical comeback, which has already included a major tour and a Billboard honor. The song and its video connect her pop career with the family-friendly world of Dr. Seuss.
